themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions in CD 314 have spiked dramatically THIS WEEK with 65 complaints versus a baseline average of 12.6 per week—a 415% increase (z-score: 16.58)—suggesting rapid pavement, pothole, or surface degradation affecting multiple blocks across Midwood/Ocean Parkway.
evidence: 65 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (415% spike)
Z-score of 16.58 indicates statistically extreme deviation
278 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (208 alterations) suggest ongoing construction that may be degrading street infrastructure
reporting_angles: Map which streets are most affected and visit them to document conditions; interview residents about impact on foot traffic and vehicle safety
Investigate whether recent construction activity (278 DOB permits) is connected to the spike—are contractors damaging streets faster than repair crews can keep up?

themes_detail.label: Noise Surge on Streets and Sidewalks
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from streets and sidewalks LAST WEEK hit 55—a 319% spike above the 13.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.02)—indicating a sudden deterioration in neighborhood quiet, likely tied to construction, street events, or new noise sources.
evidence: 55 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 13.1 weekly average (319% increase, z-score: 7.02)
Coincides with 208 active alteration permits suggesting construction noise as likely driver
Noise - Residential category (1,805 complaints over 90 days) remains high, but street-level spike suggests new source or event
reporting_angles: Survey residents and merchants along major streets (Ocean Parkway, etc.) about noise sources: construction, street fairs, traffic, or something new?
Cross-reference 311 noise spike with DOB permits to identify which construction projects are generating complaints

themes_detail.label: Sewer and Infrastructure Failures
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints LAST WEEK jumped to 19—a 311% increase from the 4.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.7)—indicating potential sewage backup, overflow, or underground infrastructure failure across the district.
evidence: 19 sewer complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.6 weekly average (311% spike, z-score: 7.7)
Street condition spike (65 complaints THIS WEEK) may indicate broken pipes or excavation for sewer repair
Potential public health concern if sewage is affecting residential areas or waterways
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with DEP for recent sewer-related emergency calls and work orders in CD 314; identify affected blocks
Interview residents about odors, backups, or surface flooding; connect to broader aging infrastructure concerns in South Brooklyn

themes_detail.label: Illegal Animals and Zoonotic Risk
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about illegal animals kept as pets surged to 3 LAST WEEK, a 2300% spike from the 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69), suggesting residents are keeping exotic, dangerous, or disease-carrying animals in residential areas.
evidence: 3 illegal animal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Extreme statistical deviation suggests a new trend or organized activity, not random incidents
Public health risk if animals carry diseases or pose safety threats to children and pets
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD and Animal Care & Control to learn what types of animals are being reported and where they're concentrated
Interview animal welfare experts about why residents might be keeping illegal animals; investigate if there's a market or social media trend driving this

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Decline and Hazmat Spill Risk
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints LAST WEEK reached 7—a 522% increase from 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 5.58)—while hazardous materials complaints 3 WEEKS AGO hit 3 (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35), suggesting environmental stress or contamination events affecting the district's green infrastructure and soil quality.
evidence: 7 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (522% spike, z-score: 5.58)
3 hazardous materials complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Street damage spike (65 THIS WEEK) may indicate soil instability or contamination affecting both trees and pavement
reporting_angles: Request Parks Department data on tree removals and soil testing results in CD 314 over past 30 days; map affected areas
Investigate what hazardous materials were reported 3 weeks ago (industrial spill, illegal dumping, etc.) and whether remediation is underway
